caveats: Official pages disagree on the default effort of Fable 5.2 and Sonnet 5.5: the API pages say high, Claude Code's model configuration page says medium. Tune always writes an effort, so no default applies to a role it manages.
Effort has no price of its own. A higher level uses more tokens at the model's price.
Anthropic gives no effort level for code review in particular; the note for a reviewer is the model's general guidance.

fable.name: Fable 5.2
fable.note: Built for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work.

opus.name: Opus 5.5
opus.note: Built for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. Early testers reported stronger code review than Opus 5: more bugs caught, fewer false alarms.

sonnet.name: Sonnet 5.5
sonnet.note: The best combination of speed and intelligence, built for everyday coding and agent work.

haiku.name: Haiku 5.5
haiku.note: For high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks, including subagent tasks. A prompt over 100,000 tokens pays five times these prices.

general.low: Most efficient: large token savings with some loss of capability. Suits simpler tasks that need speed and low cost.
general.medium: Balanced, with moderate token savings. Suits agentic tasks that weigh speed, cost and performance.
general.high: Spends as many tokens as the task needs. Suits complex reasoning, difficult coding and agentic tasks.
general.xhigh: Extended capability for long-horizon work: long-running agentic and coding tasks with token budgets in the millions.
general.max: Maximum capability with no limit on token spending. For tasks that need the deepest reasoning.

fable.low: Suits quick back-and-forth, well-specified tasks and high-volume workloads.
fable.medium: Suits interactive coding, chat and everyday knowledge work.
fable.high: Suits hard coding, research, agentic work and long unattended runs. Most of the gain in capability is already present at high.
fable.xhigh: For the hardest long-running coding and agentic work, where you have measured a gain.
fable.max: For measuring the model's ceiling, or the rare task where time and tokens don't matter.

opus.low: On several coding evaluations low comes close to Opus 5 at high, at much lower cost.
opus.medium: The starting point. At medium it matches or exceeds Opus 5 at high on coding and knowledge-work evaluations.
opus.xhigh: Reserve for work where you have measured a quality gain.
opus.max: Reserve for work where you have measured a quality gain.

sonnet.medium: The starting point for agentic coding and multistep tool use on well-specified tasks.
sonnet.high: For harder or longer agentic tasks; the step up from medium.
sonnet.xhigh: Use only where your evaluations show a quality gain.
sonnet.max: Use only where your evaluations show a quality gain.

haiku.low: Cheapest and fastest: for chat, short tool tasks and simple high-volume requests. In long agent prompts it is more likely to skip a search, stop early or skip a check.
haiku.medium: The starting point for most work, including agentic coding.
haiku.high: For knowledge work, longer agent tasks and strict instruction following.
